transcript:
Date/Time: 2026-03-06 10:00 AM PDT | Duration: ~60m
Attendees: Maya Patel (CEO), Ethan Li (CTO), Sofia Martinez (VP Product), Daniel Park (Head of Eng), Claire Nguyen (CFO), People Ops, All-hands
Slides: https://redwood.company/slides/q1-2026-all-hands (deck) | Latency dashboard: https://redwood.company/dashboards/latency (internal)

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, good morning, good afternoon, good evening, wherever you are. Um welcome to our March all hands, happy start of Q2 prep for those of you counting quarters differently. We'll keep it tight 60 minutes, we'll run through a few big updates and then open for q and a.

[00:18] Ethan Li: Quick shout on infra, we saw a 12% reduction in p99 tail lat over the last sprint, mostly thanks to the KV cache changes and some kernel selection improvements. It's not perfect but moving in the right direction.

[00:35] Sofia Martinez: On product, shipping structured output v2 next week, this includes more robust tool calling and a new schema-mapper from the console. We'll also start a limited beta for optimizer suggestions for customers on Dedicated.

[00:50] Claire Nguyen: From a finance perspective, bookings are healthy, churn is low, spend is roughly on plan — small headroom but we need to be disciplined on hiring. We'll share a hiring cadence and priorities in people ops update.

[01:05] Audience question (Slack): is SOC2 type II next on the cert list?

[01:10] Maya Patel: Yes SOC2 is in flight, we expect final audit by end of Q2, and ISO follow-up conversations are underway. All compliance docs will be in the security portal we shared.

[01:28] Daniel Park: A couple notes from Eng: Dedicated autoscaling improvements shipped in canary, we're seeing better utilization but still tuning burst policy. Also packaging for Private (VPC/on-prem) is getting simpler, tho a few customer edge cases remain.

[01:50] Engineer comment (Speaker 7): the private deploy installer had an issue with KMS integration on one of our tests, error 403 confusing, we traced it to KMS role mapping — fix is in review.

[02:12] Ethan Li: Right, there's some friction with KMS/HSM mapping in certain cloud accounts, we're adding clearer docs and a test harness for customers. We also added an automatic fallback for model variants when capacity is constrained so apps stay online without a 15s timeout pop.

[02:39] Maya Patel: On go-to-market, PLG motion is working well, self-serve growth up 25% q/q, Enterprise deals still driving ARR. We'll continue to focus on benchmarks and case studies to show production economics.

[02:55] Sofia Martinez: New features preview: streaming with structured output and function calling improvements, more deterministic token counts for cost estimation, and a small eval harness to detect regressions on rollouts. Expect a public blog post and a howto in our docs.

[03:17] Audience (Speaker 12): question re: Dedicated vs Hosted cost tradeoff — a customer asked if Dedicated always wins for cost at scale?

[03:25] Claire Nguyen: Short answer: usually Dedicated becomes more economical at sustained high throughput once you amortize reserved capacity. But there's nuance: burst patterns, model mix, and quantization profiles all change the math. We'll share a cost model spreadsheet.

[03:46] Ethan Li: Also, Redwood Optimize will offer specific quantization and batching recommendations per workload, that should tip the scales for more customers.

[04:03] Maya Patel: On reliability, we want predictable SLAs. We're investing in observability — token-level tracing, per-route dashboards, and synthetic workloads to catch regressions early.

[04:20] Daniel Park: We're adding automated rollbacks for model rollouts tied to eval regressions; so if a new model causes a drop in quality on the canary prompt set it will auto-fallback.

[04:36] Sofia Martinez: Product metrics: we track latency, cost-per-token, and quality regressions. The quality metric uses a labeled prompt set and A/B evals — it's early but useful.

[04:52] Audience (Speaker 20): question on regions — APAC infra updates?

[04:58] Ethan Li: APAC region expansion is happening, new region partner later this quarter; private customers will get region selection options in the console.

[05:12] Maya Patel: Hiring update from People Ops: we prioritize infra, product, and SE hires this quarter. We will freeze some non-critical roles to ensure runway.

[05:30] Claire Nguyen: We'll publish the headcount plan and the approved roles, folks can raise questions in the hiring thread.

[05:45] Q&A: Security deep-dive requests and benchmarking

[06:00] Speaker (Sales AE): Request from field: customers want a benchmark kit to run against their workloads for lat/cost/quality comparisons — can we produce a lightweight script and a results template?

[06:15] Ethan Li: Yes, SE team already has a prototype benchmark harness, we'll make it consumable and put it in the partner folder. Expect beta by 2026-03-20.

[06:30] Sofia Martinez: We'll also publish example prompt sets and a recommended config for batching and cache to reduce unit cost.

[06:45] Audience murmurs / clapping

[07:00] Maya Patel: Quick shoutouts — kudos to infra for the p99 improvement, to product for structured outputs, and to sales for closing two mid-market renewals.

[07:20] Closing logistics: follow up docs will be posted in #all-hands and the company wiki. Please review the OKR draft and add comments.

[07:35] Final Q: Are we still targeting the private on-prem beta for mid-May?

[07:40] Daniel Park: Mid-May target stands, contingent on a few packaging issues and KMS fixes, but we're optimistic.

[07:55] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. Action items and next steps in the meeting notes. We'll do a technical deep-dive with infra and SE next week for those interested. Meeting adjourned.

Notes: transcription includes some mis-hearings (KV cache sometimes spoken as "K-V cash"), product names occasionally truncated in auto-transcript. For deeper follow-up see linked slides and the latency/dashboard links above.
